title: A Wi-Fi clock on seven-segment digits

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Think of an old-school digital clock, the kind with glowing seven-segment digits, except this one lives on your Wi-Fi.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How does a clock join Wi-Fi without a keyboard?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the neat part. ESP32-7SEG runs on an ESP32 microcontroller. At startup, the firmware checks whether it already has saved Wi-Fi settings it can reuse. If it does, it just connects. If not, it opens a setup path so you can configure the network.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's an HTTP interface, so the display can be controlled over the network. The project also includes a mobile controller, written in Kotlin, to drive multi-digit displays.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So there's firmware and an app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Firmware in C plus plus on the board, Kotlin on the phone, with PlatformIO and Gradle for building. It's MIT licensed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. The written page walks through the startup decision and the setup flow.
